# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Nigeria, 2024: 3B.1 research note

**Bottom line:** The record is **mostly negative**. Tinubu publicly endorsed police professionalism and, after backlash, ordered the release of detained minors. But the dominant 2024 evidence is a violent protest crackdown: live ammunition, excessive force, torture, arbitrary detention, treason charges, and no clear public acceptance of responsibility for abuses.

## Accepted claims

- **Title:** [We Will Transform Nigeria Police Into Modern, Professional Force – President Tinubu](https://statehouse.gov.ng/we-will-transform-nigeria-police-into-modern-professional-force-president-tinubu/)  
  **Publisher:** State House, Abuja  
  **Date:** April 16, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Tinubu said his administration had begun reforms to make the police “modern, professional and accountable” and emphasized training and capacity-building. This is the clearest positive signal for institutional restraint, though it is aspirational rather than proof of outcomes.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`

- **Title:** [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/)  
  **Publisher:** State House, Abuja  
  **Date:** August 4, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Tinubu acknowledged deaths, destruction, and unrest, and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. This is partial acknowledgment of harm, but it does not amount to accountability for later-documented abuses.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462)  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** July 31, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported the government was open to dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence, but it shows the public line included de-escalation before the crackdown.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** [At least 3 killed in Nigeria at protests over high cost of living](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376)  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** August 1, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported at least three protesters were killed in Kaduna during the nationwide demonstrations. This is direct negative evidence for protection from state violence.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- **Title:** [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/)  
  **Publisher:** Amnesty International  
  **Date:** November 28, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Amnesty said police shot protesters with live ammunition, used tear gas dangerously, killed at least 24 people, detained over 1,200, and tortured at least one detainee. It also said the authorities denied wrongdoing despite evidence. This is the strongest evidence against protection from state violence and abuse.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- **Title:** [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason)  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** September 6, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** HRW said authorities charged protesters with treason, kept them in custody with limited access to lawyers, and held minors in conditions that raised due-process and humane-treatment concerns. This is strong evidence of arbitrary or exemplary punishment and political imprisonment risk.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- **Title:** [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000)  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** November 1, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported the government expanded treason charges to 76 people, including minors, after the August protests. This reinforces the pattern of political imprisonment and disproportionate punishment.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- **Title:** [Tinubu orders release of minors arrested during EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.icirnigeria.org/tinubu-orders-release-of-minors-arrested-during-endbadgovernance-protests/)  
  **Publisher:** ICIR Nigeria  
  **Date:** November 4, 2024  
  **Claim summary:** After public outrage, Tinubu ordered the release of minors detained over the protests. This is the clearest positive accountability item, but it came only after the abusive detention had already occurred and does not cover the broader crackdown.  
  **Question IDs:** `3B.1`, `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`

## Synthesis

For **3B.1**, the best-supported reading is:

- **Limited positive evidence:** police-reform language and a late corrective order releasing minors.
- **Dominant negative evidence:** lethal protest policing, torture, arbitrary detention, treason charges, and no clear public acceptance of responsibility for the abuses.
- **Overall:** Tinubu did **not** convincingly protect residents from state violence in 2024; the strongest evidence points the other way.

## Search gap

- I found **no direct evidence** on disappearance cases tied specifically to Tinubu’s 2024 security posture.
- I also found **no clear public inquiry, apology, or accountability process** from Tinubu for the protest killings beyond the release of minors.
